answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the ocean identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator forfeits for 264 runs and collects one. Because the garden index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the fable audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 264 answers need 264 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
